note: A ${secret:...} reference has three seams, and they refuse in three sentences: the scheme (build time) emits a marker and prefixes refusals with `resource settings expand: `, Resolve (use time) prefixes them with `resource secret: ` and wraps a backend failure into one, and the Secret value itself redacts to `<secret>` under every rendering verb.
A path is what the ${} parser hands the scheme: outer space around the colon is already trimmed by parseReference, so the rows here never contain a leading or trailing blank.
Every store in this file is a resource.SecretStoreFunc over a canned answer table: no process environment, no clock, no filesystem, so a row is a function of this file and nothing is masked.

Not covered here: the stores core ships (`env`, `file`), the strict settings decode behind them, and the wiring rules `core/deploy` applies (id fallback to the resource name, duplicate ids, one default). Those come with the store tables.
Every refusal below is a validation error; the wrapping of a backend failure is the one that looks like it should be a not_available and is not.
masked: nothing runtime-dependent: the stores are canned answer tables, so no sentence here depends on the run

the escaping spelling of `wire`: core writes it with json.Marshal, which HTML-escapes `<`, `>` and `&`, and the port writes it with serde_json, which does not. Both decode to the string "<secret>", so the replay compares the decoded value and not the bytes

refs.name: default-and-named
refs.why: a dotted prefix naming a configured store is an explicit store reference; anything else falls back to the default store whole, so dotted secret names stay addressable

refs.name: no-default
refs.why: a named store resolves without a default, and a NAME-only reference is refused rather than guessed

answers.error: resource settings expand: secret reference ${secret:TOKEN} needs an explicit store or a default secret.Store
resource settings expand: secret reference ${secret:.TOKEN} needs an explicit store or a default secret.Store

refs.name: empty-name
refs.why: the store prefix matches before the name is validated, so `files.` is the empty-name refusal; a lone dot has no prefix at all and is a name in the default store

answers.error: resource settings expand: secret name is empty
resource settings expand: secret name is empty

refs.name: prefix-without-default
refs.why: an unconfigured dotted prefix is not a refusal about the store: the whole path becomes the name of a default-store reference, and with no default the answer is the missing-default sentence

answers.error: resource settings expand: secret reference ${secret:vault.token} needs an explicit store or a default secret.Store

resolves.name: value
resolves.why: a found secret comes back verbatim, newlines and all

resolves.name: missing
resolves.why: a store that has no such secret is a refusal naming both the secret and the store, not an empty value
resolves.error: resource secret: "NOPE" not found in store "env"

resolves.name: store-failure
resolves.why: a backend failure is wrapped verbatim into a validation sentence instead of being reclassified as not_available
resolves.error: resource secret: store "env": backend is down

resolves.name: unconfigured-store
resolves.why: resolving through an id that was never configured is refused before any store is asked
resolves.error: resource secret: store "vault" is not configured

resolves.name: no-resolver
resolves.why: a Secret handed to a factory with no Input.Secrets refuses with the same sentence shape, naming the secret it could not resolve

values.name: literal
values.why: a plain string is a literal secret: not a reference, and resolvable with no resolver at all

values.name: literal-empty
values.why: the empty string is a literal too, not an absent value

values.name: literal-blank
values.why: a literal of spaces is kept as written: blank is refused for a reference, never for a literal

values.name: reference
values.why: a reference object decodes to a lazy reference and resolves through its store at use time

values.name: reference-extra-field
values.why: unknown fields in a reference object are ignored, because core decodes it with a plain json.Unmarshal

values.name: reference-unconfigured-store
values.why: a reference decodes without checking the store exists; the refusal arrives at use time
values.resolve_error: resource secret: store "vault" is not configured

values.name: reference-missing-secret
values.why: an empty lookup is a use-time refusal, not an empty value
values.resolve_error: resource secret: "NOPE" not found in store "env"

values.name: reference-no-store
values.why: a reference object without a store is refused at decode time, and blank counts as absent
values.error: resource secret: reference must carry store and name

values.name: reference-blank-store
values.why: a store of spaces is blank after trimming
values.error: resource secret: reference must carry store and name

values.name: reference-blank-name
values.why: a name of tabs is blank after trimming
values.error: resource secret: reference must carry store and name

values.name: reference-case-folded-fields
values.why: reference field names match case-insensitively, which is encoding/json's rule and not a choice of core's

values.name: reference-null-field
values.why: a null field is the same no-op it is for a plain string, so it leaves that half of the reference blank
values.error: resource secret: reference must carry store and name

values.name: reference-number-field
values.why: a field of the wrong type fails the struct decode, so the shape refusal quotes the document rather than calling the field blank
values.error: resource secret: want string or {"store":...,"name":...}, got {"store":5,"name":"TOKEN"}

values.name: null
values.why: null unmarshals into the string branch as a no-op, so it is the empty literal -- not a reference, not the blank-reference refusal, and not the wrong-shape one

values.name: empty-object
values.why: an empty object decodes into the reference struct and leaves it zero, so it is the blank-reference refusal
values.error: resource secret: reference must carry store and name

values.name: number
values.why: a scalar that is not a string is the wrong-shape refusal, and it quotes the document as written
values.error: resource secret: want string or {"store":...,"name":...}, got 5

values.name: array
values.why: an array is the wrong-shape refusal too, quoted as written
values.error: resource secret: want string or {"store":...,"name":...}, got [1, 2]

values.name: bool
values.why: a boolean is the wrong-shape refusal, quoted as written
values.error: resource secret: want string or {"store":...,"name":...}, got true

values.name: literal-no-resolver
values.why: a literal short-circuits before the resolver, so a factory with no Input.Secrets still reads its own literal

values.name: reference-no-resolver
values.why: a reference with no resolver is refused, naming the secret

stores.name: env-default
stores.why: the env store reads the process environment by the name the reference gives it, and reports a missing variable as not-found rather than as a failure

stores.name: env-id
stores.why: id and default come from the settings, and an absent id means the deployment resource's name is used instead -- the store answers no id

stores.name: file-base-required
stores.why: a file store without a base directory is refused at build time, before any lookup
stores.error: secret file store: settings.base is required

stores.name: file-token
stores.why: a file store reads one file per secret and strips the trailing newline a `printf` or `echo` leaves, so a key stored as a line works

lookups.name: ../secret
lookups.error: resource loader: file source "../secret" escapes base dir

lookups.name: /etc/passwd
lookups.error: resource loader: file source "/etc/passwd" must be relative

stores.name: file-cap
stores.why: the loader caps what it will read, and a file over the cap is a refusal rather than a truncated secret

stores.name: file-id
stores.why: a file store carries its id and default flag from the settings, like the env store

stores.name: file-blank-base
stores.why: a base directory of spaces is blank after trimming, so it is missing rather than a path
stores.error: secret file store: settings.base is required

stores.name: file-null-base
stores.why: a null field leaves its scalar untouched, which is encoding/json's rule for every type -- so a null base is the same missing base, not a shape refusal
stores.error: secret file store: settings.base is required

stores.name: env-unknown-field
stores.why: settings decode strictly, so a typo is refused instead of silently dropped -- and the part of the sentence that is core's is the prefix
stores.error_prefix: secret env store: decode settings: resource settings decode: resource settings:

stores.name: file-unknown-field
stores.why: the same strictness in the other store's struct: one row per settings type, because a typo in one proves nothing about the other
stores.error_prefix: secret file store: decode settings: resource settings decode: resource settings:
